objectives.label: Sample space and probability
objectives.description: Write the sample space and events of a random experiment as sets and calculate the probability P(A) = n(A)/n(S).

objectives.label: Intersection and mutually exclusive
objectives.description: Determine the intersection A ∩ B of two events using a Venn diagram, calculate its probability, and identify mutually exclusive events.

objectives.label: Union of events
objectives.description: Determine the union A ∪ B of two events and calculate its probability using P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B), including for mutually exclusive events.

entries.text: Picture of a dice showing faces 4, 3 and 1.

A.why: A dice picture illustrates the random experiment whose sample space is written.

B.why: Dice picture introduces the random experiment whose sample space is written.

entries.text: n(A) is the number of elements of the event A, n(S) is the number of elements of sample space S, and P(A) is the probability of occurring event A.

A.why: Defines n(A), n(S) and P(A) used in P(A)=n(A)/n(S).

B.why: Defines n(A), n(S) and P(A), the notation for P(A) = n(A)/n(S).

entries.text: Number line of probability: impossible event at 0 (0%); less likely at 1/4 (25%); equally likely as unlikely at 1/2 (50%); more likely at 3/4 (75%); certain event at 1 (100%).

A.why: Probability number line shows the range of values of P(A).

B.why: Probability number line gives the meaning of probability values from 0 to 1.

entries.text: Spinner circle divided into eight equal sectors with a pointer; colours going clockwise from the top: green, yellow, green, yellow, (bottom) green, yellow? read from image: top-right green, right-upper yellow, right-lower green, bottom-right yellow, bottom-left green, left-lower blue, left-upper peach (light orange), top-left orange. Pointer stops in the peach sector.

A.why: Spinner experiment is used to write sample space and events.

B.why: Spinner is a random experiment whose sample space and events are written as sets.

entries.text: Venn diagram in a rectangle labelled E: two overlapping circles B (left) and A (right); the overlap is shaded and labelled with an arrow 'B ∩ A'.

A.why: Venn diagram with shaded overlap shows the intersection B ∩ A.

B.why: Shaded overlap labelled B ∩ A illustrates the intersection of two events.

entries.text: Note that: It is said that an event occurred if the outcome of the experiment is an element of the elements of the set expressing this event.

A.why: Explains when an event occurs, based on the outcome being an element of the event set.

B.why: States when an event occurs, based on the outcome being an element of the event set.

entries.text: Eight identical plain green-yellow cards in two rows of four, no numbers shown.

A.why: Identical cards form the experiment whose sample space and events are written.

B.why: Cards for a random experiment, used to set up the sample space and events.

entries.text: Venn diagram in rectangle S with circle B and circle A; intersection of A and B shaded yellow containing 2; B only contains 3, 5, 7; A only contains 6, 8 and 4 (4 and 8 inside a smaller oval C inside A); points marked x. Read from figure; verify.

A.why: Venn diagram with shaded intersection of A and B and an event C, used for intersection and exclusivity.

B.why: Venn diagram with shaded intersection of A and B, and the smaller oval C inside A.

entries.text: The two events B and C cannot occur at the same time so we say A and B are mutually exclusive events.

A.why: States that events which cannot occur together are mutually exclusive.

B.why: Explains that events which cannot occur together are mutually exclusive.

entries.text: A set of events is mutually exclusive if every pair of them is mutually exclusive.

A.why: Extends mutually exclusive to a set of events.

B.why: Defines a set of mutually exclusive events.

entries.text: Two separate (non-overlapping) ovals labelled A (yellow) and B (green), showing mutually exclusive events.

A.why: Separate ovals illustrate mutually exclusive events.

B.why: Non-overlapping ovals show mutually exclusive events.

entries.text: Venn diagram inside rectangle S with two overlapping circles. Left circle labelled B contains 3, 9 and the overlap 6 (shaded yellow); right circle labelled A contains 2, 4, 8 and the overlap 6. Outside both circles: 5, 1, and 7 which is circled in green and labelled C.

A.why: Venn diagram with overlap 6 and disjoint C is used to find intersections and mutually exclusive events.

B.why: Venn diagram with overlap 6 and separate C is used to find the intersection and mutually exclusive events.

entries.text: Venn diagram in a rectangle labelled S with two separate (disjoint) ovals labelled A and B.

A.why: Disjoint ovals show mutually exclusive events A and B.

B.why: Disjoint ovals A and B show mutually exclusive events.

entries.text: Remark: if A and B are mutually exclusive events from sample space S (as in the figure), then the following hold.

A.why: Remark on properties of mutually exclusive events, about their intersection.

B.why: Remark on properties of mutually exclusive events, starting with the empty intersection.

entries.text: For mutually exclusive events, A ∩ B is the empty set. $A \cap B = \phi$

A.why: Mutually exclusive events have an empty intersection.

B.why: Mutually exclusive events have A ∩ B = φ.

entries.text: P(A ∩ B) = (number of elements of φ)/(number of elements of S) = Zero/(number of elements of S) = Zero. $P(A \cap B)=\frac{n(\phi)}{n(S)}=\frac{0}{n(S)}=0$

A.why: Shows the probability of the intersection of mutually exclusive events is zero.

B.why: Probability of the intersection of mutually exclusive events is zero.

entries.text: Venn diagram in rectangle S with overlapping ovals A and B and a separate oval C. A only: 1, 3, 4; overlap A∩B: 7; B only: 2, 5; outside ovals: 8; C contains 6, 9, 12. C is disjoint from A and B.

A.why: Venn diagram with overlap A∩B and disjoint C practises intersection and mutually exclusive events.

B.why: Venn diagram with disjoint C and overlapping A, B illustrates intersection and mutually exclusive events.

lessons.title: Complementary event and the difference between two events

objectives.label: Complementary event and its probability
objectives.description: Determine the complementary event A` of an event A in a sample space S (A ∪ A` = S, A ∩ A` = φ) and calculate P(A`) using P(A`) = 1 - P(A).

objectives.label: Difference between two events
objectives.description: Calculate the probability of the difference between two events, A - B (the occurrence of A only), from set counts or a Venn diagram, using (A - B) ∪ (A ∩ B) = A.

entries.text: Venn diagram: rectangle labelled S containing an oval labelled A; the region outside the oval is labelled A`.

A.why: Venn diagram shows A and its complement A` in S.

B.why: Venn diagram showing A in S with A` as the region outside it.

entries.text: The event and the complementary event are two mutually exclusive events.

A.why: States that an event and its complement are mutually exclusive, part of the complementary event.

B.why: Says an event and its complement are mutually exclusive (A ∩ A` = φ).

entries.text: Drill table to complete: events A and A`, probabilities, and their sum; some cells given, others blank. event A, event A`, P (A), P (A`), P (A) + P (A`) / {2, 4, 6}, , , , / , {3, 6}, , , / {5}, , , , / {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, , , ,

A.why: Drill on A, A`, P(A), P(A`) and their sum of 1.

B.why: Drill table on A, A`, P(A), P(A`) and their sum, which is 1.

entries.text: Venn diagram in rectangle S with two overlapping ovals labelled B (left) and A (right). Left-only region 7, intersection 8, right-only region 10, outside both ovals 15. Values read from the figure; verify.

A.why: Venn diagram with set counts used to find the probability of A - B.

B.why: Venn diagram with counts used to find the probability of A - B.

entries.text: The set A - B (reading Al Akhbar only, not the other newspaper) is read as 'A difference B'. $A-B$

A.why: Defines A - B as A only, read 'A difference B'.

B.why: Defines A - B as 'A difference B', reading Al Akhbar only.

entries.text: Venn diagram in rectangle S with two overlapping ovals, B (left) and A (right). The part of A outside B is shaded blue and labelled A - B.

A.why: Shaded Venn diagram showing A - B as the part of A outside B.

B.why: Venn diagram shading A - B, the part of A outside B.

entries.text: Note that (A - B) ∪ (A ∩ B) = A (the symbol between the two brackets is not clearly printed). $(A - B) \cup (A \cap B) = A$

A.why: Gives (A - B) ∪ (A ∩ B) = A for the difference of two events.

B.why: States (A - B) ∪ (A ∩ B) = A, the identity for the difference of two events.
